item.title: Anthropic's report smells a lot like bullshit
UK's first small nuclear power station to be built in north Wales
item.description:
📝 Visiting a further education college in north Wales on Thursday, Sir Keir said the development would bring jobs for "decades to come" and that work would begin "virtually straight away". Mims Davies MP, the Shadow Secretary of State for Wales, said it will bring much-needed jobs and investment but "the current plan will only generate a fraction of the power that a Gigawatt-powered plant would". The company will report back by autumn 2026, officials said.
🔗 Read more: https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c051y3d7myzo

item.title: Facebook Text Log Between Mark Zuckerberg and Kevin Systrom(Instagram Cofounder)
Bypassing the Branch Predictor
item.description:
📝 Those attributes will typically just reorder some labels/paths around to make sure that the path which we mark as [[likely]] will require less jumps. L2: pop rbx jmp abandon(Transaction*) It won’t really matter that the send() branch doesn’t need to do the jump at line 7, because the branch predictor will be primed to assume the abandon() branch nonetheless. We have to do this enough times such that the mocked transaction data becomes the vast majority over the real data, so the branch predictor will be primed to assume that the send() path will be executed practically on every resolve() call.
🔗 Read more: https://nicula.xyz/2025/03/10/bypassing-the-branch-predictor.html

item.title: An exposed .git folder let us dox a phishing campaign
item.description:
📝 This past Friday afternoon, a member in our Discord server reported a phishing email pointing to a fake login page. With the source code, repo and the active Telegram bot token, we filed detailed abuse reports:- GitHub: We reported the repository containing the phishing kit's source code. The crowdsourced speed and collaboration helped us take this down very fast.
🔗 Read more: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=45943802

item.title: Is our death from a hydrogen sulfide event inevitable in climate warming? (2005)
item.description:
📝 These bacteria strip oxygen from the compounds and produce hydrogen sulfide. Hydrogen sulfide kills aerobic organisms. The hydrogen sulfide dispersing in the atmosphere would kill most terrestrial life.
